paires.mention: Biais conditionnel : écart des scores du classement (base − cotation) ; au-delà de ±1, haussier ou baissier conditionnel.

projections: Given the ongoing resilience of the global economy, the Bank has revised up global GDP growth slightly to 3.1% in 2026, while growth in 2027 and 2028 remains unchanged from the July projection at 3.2%.
The Canadian economy is expected to grow 1% in 2026, and 2% in 2027 and 2028.
Given persistently high oil prices, CPI inflation has been around 3% since April and is expected to rise to about 3½% by the end of the year.

deliberations.titre: Summary of Governing Council deliberations: Fixed announcement date of October 28, 2026
options: Given the persistence of higher energy prices, members spent considerable time discussing how this shock was raising costs for Canadian businesses.

Governing Council discussed the historical lags from costs to consumer prices and reflected on the Bank’s surveys in which businesses had reported that they anticipated passing on more of these cost increases to their customers.
Governing Council members deliberated two options: maintain the policy rate at 2.25% or raise the policy rate to 2.5%.
suite: Cost pressures were building, and while businesses had so far mostly absorbed higher input costs, past experience and Bank surveys suggested that cost pass‑through would increase over the next year.

Governing Council members agreed there could be a need to increase the policy rate further, but given the uncertainty, they would take monetary policy decisions one meeting at a time with the benefit of the best available information.
projections: Overall, members revised up their outlook for growth in 2026 to 1% and expected growth to strengthen to 2% in 2027 and 2028.
CPI inflation was expected to rise to 3½% at the end of 2026 and remain above 3% through much of 2027, before gradually declining to the 2% target by the middle of 2028.
